calendar_system: Lunisolar calendar (months pegged to moon cycle, leap month Adar II added 7 times in 19 years to keep Pesach in the spring).

holidays.name: Pesach (Passover)
holidays.biblical_origin: Exodus 12: liberation from Egypt, sacrifice of paschal lamb.
holidays.rabbinic_development: Seder night, eating Matzah and Maror, recitation of the Haggadah, four cups of wine.
holidays.modern_observance: Celebrated worldwide by all denominations as festival of freedom and national birth.

holidays.name: Shavuot (Feast of Weeks)
holidays.biblical_origin: Exodus 23, 34; Leviticus 23: Feast of first fruits (Bikkurim) and wheat harvest 50 days after Pesach.
holidays.rabbinic_development: Zman Matan Torateinu (Time of the Giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai), all-night Torah study (Tikkun Leil Shavuot), reading Book of Ruth.

holidays.name: Sukkot (Feast of Booths)
holidays.biblical_origin: Leviticus 23: dwelling in temporary booths commemorating wilderness wanderings.
holidays.observance: Dwelling in Sukkah, waving Four Species (Arba'at Ha-Minim: Etrog, Lulav, Hadas, Aravah), followed by Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah.

holidays.name: Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year)
holidays.biblical_origin: Leviticus 23:24: Yom Teru'ah (Day of Shofar Blasting).
holidays.rabbinic_development: Yom Ha-Din (Day of Judgment for all creatures), sounding 100 blasts of the ram's horn, dipping apples in honey.

holidays.name: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)
holidays.biblical_origin: Leviticus 16 & 23: Sabbath of Sabbaths, ritual purgation of sanctuary.
holidays.rabbinic_development: 25-hour complete fast from food, drink, washing, leather shoes, and marital relations; extensive communal confession (Al Chet) and final Ne'ilah service.

holidays.name: Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)
holidays.origin: Historical Second Temple victory (164 BCE) of Maccabees over Seleucid Syrian-Greeks and rededication of the Temple.
holidays.observance: Kindling 8-branched Menorah (Hanukkiah), eating oil-fried foods (latkes, sufganiyot) commemorating the miracle of the oil flask.

holidays.name: Purim
holidays.date: 14 Adar (15 Adar in walled cities / Shushan Purim)
holidays.origin: Book of Esther: deliverance of Persian Jews from Haman's genocide decree.
holidays.observance: Reading Megillat Esther, sending gifts of food (Mishloach Manot), charity to the poor (Matanot La-Evyonim), festive meal.
